verdict_scope: The frozen draft remains useful as non-authorizing implementation evidence, but the reviewed native helper, tests, allowlist, validator, and validator tests do not yet qualify a production component or justify a sealed launcher.

positive_counterevidence.evidence: The helper exposes only a test-only schema/backend, marks production_eligible and effect_authorized false, returns a nonserializable process-local lease, and has no collect_production entry point.
require_process_running correctly treats WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0) == WAIT_TIMEOUT as running, rejects other results, and rechecks the Windows process creation token.

Target and sentinel leaves are opened relative to retained parent handles, FileIdInfo and FileStandardInfo are recorded, reparse leaves are rejected, link_count must equal one, duplicate file identities fail, and file identity/hash are rechecked before record sealing.

The record limits its positive claim to governed-byte and directory-member delta and explicitly reports metadata/cloud-hydration proof unavailable, process inventory non-exhaustive, writer exclusion false, and production readiness false.

validate_files pins both the current allowlist bytes and the source V6 manifest bytes to exact SHA-256 values before object validation, checks exact 13/3 counts and order, and protects the current path/hash/size tuple against file drift.

findings.challenge: The exported competing_open_denied(path) primitive has no safe-root check and accepts any caller-supplied filesystem path. It requests GENERIC_WRITE or DELETE access before proving that the path is inside the disposable nonce root. A caller can therefore direct this test-only module at canonical or global files, contradicting the claimed canonical/global nonaccess boundary even if no bytes are ultimately written.
findings.counterevidence: The frozen tests call this function only on a generated sentinel below a UUID-named C:\tmp fixture, and the function performs only an open/close contention probe.
findings.required_resolution: Make the primitive incapable of accepting an unverified path: bind it to a verified retained test-root/parent handle and exact allowed leaf, or keep it private behind a closure that already possesses the verified fixture lease. Add an adversarial canonical/outside-root rejection test before any open.
findings.appeal: A test caller may promise to pass only fixture paths, but caller discipline is not the corrected design's fail-closed safety boundary.

findings.challenge: Safe-root, workspace, parent-membership, and cleanup continuity are not fully handle-rooted. verify_safe_test_root resolves a pathname but retains no root handle; workspace is later opened by full pathname; directory membership is enumerated again by model/path strings; final validation rechecks only target/sentinel and process handles; and cleanup revalidates only the pathname pattern before shutil.rmtree. A rename/substitution can separate the retained objects from the path later enumerated or deleted.
findings.counterevidence: Model, nested parent, and file leaves are initially opened with NT RootDirectory semantics, their handles are retained, and reparse/identity alias checks reduce substitution risk.
findings.required_resolution: Retain and freeze the exact test-root handle identity; open workspace relative to it; enumerate memberships through retained directory handles; revalidate volume/root/workspace/model/all parent identities plus exact handle leaf-parent relations immediately before sealing; and require cleanup to compare the retained root identity to the current cleanup target before deletion.
findings.appeal: UUID naming makes accidental collision unlikely, but likelihood is not identity continuity and does not close a fail-closed cleanup race.

findings.challenge: Process evidence is an ancestry sample, not the corrected design's bounded relational closure. The Toolhelp snapshot supplies name and parent_pid; a later OpenProcess validates only that the newly opened PID is live and has a stable creation token. The code does not bind the snapshot name/parent relation to that opened instance, does not hash the executable, stops after a default depth of three, does not enumerate/classify the complete bounded writer set, and cannot reject hidden OneDrive/other writer rows. PID reuse between snapshot and handle acquisition remains ambiguous.
findings.counterevidence: Every sampled ancestor is opened with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION plus SYNCHRONIZE, its executable is opened and identified, WAIT_TIMEOUT is correctly required, and its creation token is checked twice.
findings.required_resolution: Implement exact bounded enumeration and code-fixed classification; bind snapshot rows to opened instances using PID plus creation time plus executable identity/hash and revalidated parent relation; fail on inaccessible/partial rows; and add access-denied, exit-during-capture, PID-reuse, ancestry contradiction, and hidden-writer negatives.
findings.appeal: The helper honestly labels process_inventory_exhaustive false, so this is not evidence fraud; it is nevertheless insufficient for component qualification.

findings.challenge: native_architecture is read from the mutable PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE environment variable rather than a native Windows architecture API. The record can therefore misdescribe host architecture while presenting it as an operating-system fact.
findings.counterevidence: The helper is explicitly test-only and also records Python pointer width.
findings.required_resolution: Use GetNativeSystemInfo and/or IsWow64Process2 with exact API error handling, record native and process architecture separately, and test environment-variable spoofing cannot affect the fact.
findings.appeal: Environment architecture is useful diagnostic metadata but cannot satisfy the corrected design's exact OS/build/architecture gate.

findings.challenge: The effects record states canonical_or_global_path_opened=false although collection opens the volume-root GUID and current/ancestor executable image paths outside the disposable fixture. This conflates 'no canonical target opened' with 'no global/system path opened' and makes the nonaccess claim broader than the observed behavior.
findings.counterevidence: No canonical Hosea target or global sidecar is derived or opened by collect_test_only_temp_root, and all reported mutation flags remain false.
findings.required_resolution: Split the claim into exact categories: canonical governed target opened, disposable fixture opened, volume metadata/root opened, and process executable opened. Mark the latter two true and keep zero-delta evidence scoped only to the fixture bytes and enumerated memberships.
findings.appeal: If 'global' was intended to mean only the three global sidecars, rename the field; the current wording remains materially ambiguous.

findings.challenge: The native tests do not exercise the production primitive required by the Windows design because no production entry point exists. They also omit integrated collector rejection for reparse components, parent/root rename substitution, cleanup identity substitution, target write/delete contention, process access uncertainty, process exit, PID reuse, partial inventory, and executable-identity ambiguity. The reparse test observes a link directly rather than proving collect_test_only_temp_root rejects one in an allowed token chain.
findings.counterevidence: The frozen suite does cover actual NTFS collection, fixture byte/member equality, sentinel sharing denial, distinct identities, explicit reparse coverage_unavailable, unsafe-root rejection, exact pinned hashes, and extra-hardlink rejection. The draft freeze reports seven direct Windows functions passing while explicitly refusing to call formal pytest coverage a pass.
findings.required_resolution: Add the missing deterministic and safe real-Windows adversarial cases against the same primitive intended for production, then obtain fresh formal harness evidence or retain coverage_unavailable.
findings.appeal: Direct-function success remains useful draft evidence but is lower-grade than isolated formal tests and does not cover the missing failure paths.

findings.challenge: The allowlist validator pins the current file bytes but does not independently validate several semantic fields it presents as governed: exact application_family; normalization booleans; source_render generation and independent-content-pass hash; exact target IDs and roles; exact sentinel IDs and roles; trailing-dot/space rejection; and case-insensitive Windows path uniqueness. validate_objects therefore does not defend the declared semantic contract if reused with newly pinned bytes.
findings.counterevidence: For this exact frozen generation, validate_files rejects any byte change to the allowlist or V6 source manifest before semantic parsing, and path/hash/size/order/count relations for the current rows are checked.
findings.required_resolution: Close and validate every declared semantic subobject and exact role/ID tuple; enforce Windows casefold uniqueness and all claimed normalization rules; reject duplicate JSON keys; and add one negative per protected semantic field.
findings.appeal: A whole-file hash is strong identity evidence, but it proves that reviewed bytes are unchanged—not that every claim inside those bytes is semantically valid.

findings.challenge: Five of the 13 allowlisted transaction targets have identical preimage and staged hashes/sizes: ordinals 4, 6, 9, 11, and 13. Treating unchanged objects as forward-replacement targets adds replacement exposure without a byte-state transition and blurs the distinction between mutation targets and immutable guarded members.
findings.counterevidence: The V3 contract currently freezes an exact 13-target tuple inherited from the V6 content manifest, so retaining all 13 may be intentional for set-level completeness and validation.
findings.required_resolution: Before any launcher draft, explicitly rule whether unchanged rows are guarded non-replacement members or intentional no-op targets. If retained as targets, the kernel must skip replacement when preimage equals staged and prove that no rename/write occurred while still validating the row.
findings.appeal: Changing the 13-target tuple would itself require a new reviewed static allowlist and design-bound freeze; this review does not authorize that change.

preserved_appeals.position: The test-only helper can remain useful without satisfying production closure.
preserved_appeals.treatment: ACCEPTED. Repairing test-scope safety and claim precision is still required, but a separate sealed production adapter remains the later qualification gate.

preserved_appeals.position: Exact frozen whole-file hashes make semantic field checks redundant.
preserved_appeals.treatment: REJECTED FOR REUSABLE_VALIDATOR_CLAIMS. Hashes prove identity; semantic validation independently proves the meaning required before a new freeze.

preserved_appeals.position: Compatible retained handles and current tests sufficiently exclude writers.
preserved_appeals.treatment: REJECTED. The corrected design's strict writer-race dissent remains unresolved, and the current process inventory is explicitly non-exhaustive.

preserved_appeals.position: The exact 13-target tuple must remain unchanged even where staged bytes equal preimage bytes.
preserved_appeals.treatment: UNRESOLVED_FOR_BOSS_OR_HUMAN. Preserve the tuple until a new reviewed design decides guard-only versus explicit no-op treatment.

required_next_gate: Repair the unsafe exported path probe and make all fixture cleanup/root continuity identity-bound.
Implement complete fail-closed process relational closure and native architecture measurement.
Strengthen allowlist semantic validation and negative tests.
Resolve unchanged target treatment without silently changing the frozen tuple.
Freeze a new acyclic draft and obtain fresh independent checker, premortem, and boss review.
